lesson: In genus 1 every symmetric function of the Frobenius eigenvalues is linear in the traces, so any squared signal is trivially an intersection-form square (deg[m] = m^2) and the test separates nothing: fakes with off-line zeros and the Liouville-twisted target pass. The Hodge index theorem acts on the squared signal only as an upper bound (Weil bound for the target), the opposite side from what the low input needs. Model targets must have genus >= 2 before a "square" identity carries positivity content; there the Moebius signal is the trace on Sym^N H^1 with 1/L' weights, not a Weil functional.
